answer: Each identity must lock collateral in an escrow, so splitting control across k coordinated identities does not dilute accountability: correlated equivocation incurs penalties scaling as O(k²). Detection also activates asymmetric depreciation across the swarm’s bonded capital, making aggregate loss compound with an exponential multiplier as k grows. A plume of identities therefore offers no cheap cover; its shared signal of coordination can turn into a gale of capital loss.
